claims.text: Rapid quenching stabilizes a dual-phase microstructure in FeCoNiTi.
The stabilized microstructure contains a ferromagnetic fcc phase and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
Coexistence of the fcc and C14 phases substantially increases coercivity through spin-canted domain-wall pinning.
Nominally equiatomic as-cast FeCoNiTi already contains both fcc and C14 Laves phases.
Arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth provides the rapid quenching needed to lock in the dual-phase microstructure.
Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 is a C14-dominant comparator.
The fcc phase has an approximate composition of Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6.
The C14 Laves phase has an approximate composition of Fe27.3Co26.6Ni17.4Ti28.7.
There is antiferromagnetic coupling between the Fe/Co/Ni sublattice and the Ti sublattice in the dual-phase alloy.
This antiferromagnetic coupling reduces the overall saturation magnetization.
A boosted orbital moment in the fcc phase enhances domain-wall pinning.
Interphase interaction causes ferromagnetic ordering at 1084 K in the fcc phase.
The dual-phase system has an additional magnetic transition near 168 K.
The proposed magnetic mechanisms and transitions collectively elevate the coercive field.
The dual-phase alloy will have coercivity significantly above 100 Oe.
The coercive field will approach approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys and related derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys and related derivatives have limited orbital-moment contributions.
Pure single-phase fcc or pure C14 alloys will not exhibit the same high coercivity as the dual-phase alloy.
Pure single-phase fcc or pure C14 alloys will not exhibit the same multi-transition magnetic profile as the dual-phase alloy.

contradictions.description: Measurements are bounded at 400 K, but the experiment proposes identifying a magnetic transition at 1084 K; that transition cannot be directly established within the stated measurement range.
The nominal equiatomic FeCoNiTi alloy and Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 are called compositionally matched, although their Ni and Ti concentrations differ substantially.

The initial as-cast state is already specified as dual phase, while rapid quenching is presented as the intervention that stabilizes that same state; no distinct unquenched state is defined to isolate the intervention's effect.
